motive: Recovery of money under coercion and pressure
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the fact that respondent no.6 was aware of the complaint made by the appellant and that the FIR lodged in July 2022 suffered from an unexplained delay of three years.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as unreliable, noting that both parties failed to provide relevant documents and call records during the enquiry, which cast doubt on the credibility of their statements.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: April 2019; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: 11.07.2023; Supreme Court decision: 19 February 2024
legal_representation: Sameer Shrivastava, Dr. Sangeeta Verma, Shivendra Dixit, Advs. for the Appellants; Gautam Narayan, Ms. Asmita Singh, Harshit Goel, Sujay Jain, Sachin Patil, Kailas Bajirao Autade, Sunil Kumar Sethi, Advs. for the Respondents
investigation_status: FIR lodged on 27.07.2022; Enquiry conducted and report submitted to Sub-Divisional Officer; Investigation continued
appeal_history: Trial court: Not stated; High Court: Dismissed the writ petition; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed
prosecution_argument: The State and respondents argued that a cognizable offence was disclosed in the FIR and the High Court rightly dismissed the petition. The investigation must be allowed to continue, and if the police report finds the appellant prima facie guilty, the appellant would have adequate remedies to challenge the charge sheet.
defence_argument: The appellant submitted that the FIR was mala fide and an abuse of the process of law, lodged after an unexplained delay of three years. The FIR was a counterblast to resist the appellant from recovering the amount paid to the respondent, and the alleged transaction was not substantiated.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the police should exercise heightened caution in disputes involving unethical transactions between private parties, and that the object of the FIR must be examined to determine if it is for criminal prosecution or for recovery of money under coercion.
